Governor Ivey Selects Bill Cole to Serve on Alabama Supreme Court

November 24, 2026

Press Releases

Share

MONTGOMERY –
 Governor Kay Ivey on Tuesday announced she has selected William “Bill” Cole to serve on the Alabama Supreme Court. After President Donald Trump tapped Governor Ivey-appointee Bill Lewis last year, he has once again chosen from the Alabama Supreme Court to fill another federal judgeship. Cole now fills the vacancy left by Greg Cook who was officially sworn in as judge on the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama yesterday.

Cole comes to the Alabama Supreme Court with extensive judicial experience, most recently serving on the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals since 2019. He also served as the Chief Judge of the Alabama Court of the Judiciary.

“Bill Cole is well known to the people of Alabama, and he brings decades of judicial experience to our state’s Supreme Court,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “Over the years, he has represented clients at all levels – including at the United States Supreme Court – which will allow him to effectively serve on our state’s highest court. Alabama is a state that ensures justice is served, and Bill’s vast experience with criminal cases, in particular, make him exceptionally qualified to serve the people of our state.”

For more than two decades, Cole has served the people of Alabama. In 2005, Cole was appointed to serve as Jefferson County Circuit Judge and was subsequently elected twice by the citizens of Jefferson County to serve six-year terms as a judge in the Criminal Division. As a circuit court judge, he presided over thousands of criminal cases and more than 175 felony jury trials.

“I am honored that Governor Ivey has selected me to serve on the Alabama Supreme Court,” 
said Cole.
 “I know how much she loves our state and she has a history of appointing excellent judges and justices. With that in mind, I am proud that she has the confidence in me to ask me to serve in this important position. After serving as a circuit court judge and as a judge on the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals for over 20 years, I am excited to accept this new responsibility. Having been born and raised in Alabama and having developed a love for the law at an early age, I cannot think of any higher honor than being able to serve the people of the state of Alabama as a member our Supreme Court.”

His legal career began in private practice where he had cases involving criminal, civil, domestic relations, family and probate law. Cole is a member of the Birmingham Bar Association, the Alabama Bar Association and the American Bar Association. He served for years as a member of the Advisory Council to the Alabama Sentencing Commission and has represented the Alabama Circuit Judges Association on the Victim Notification Implementation Task Force. He is also a member of the Kiwanis Club of Birmingham and is active in many clubs and organizations.

Cole is a Birmingham, Alabama native and a graduate of Vanderbilt University and The University of Alabama School of Law. Governor Ivey’s appointment of Cole to the Alabama Supreme Court is effective immediately.

To fill Cole’s vacancy on the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals, Governor Ivey also announced today she is tapping Ben Baxley to serve. Baxley currently serves Elmore County as District Court Judge.

“Ben Baxley continues stepping up to serve the state of Alabama and offer his adept judicial expertise,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “When I tapped Ben to the District Court in Elmore County, he answered the call and has been very effective. I know he will continue serving our state well on the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals.”

As District Court Judge, Baxley’s Stay in the Game truancy initiative reduced school absenteeism in Elmore County by more than 40 percent.

Baxley began his legal career in 1990 as Assistant District Attorney in Tuscaloosa County where he handled drug prosecutions. In 1995, he became Chief Deputy District Attorney for DeKalb and Cherokee counties, where he prosecuted drug cases and major crimes of violence. There, he was instrumental in creating the Partnership for a Drug-Free DeKalb County. In 2007, he was appointed as prosecutor for the Alabama Attorney General’s Office handling public corruption and violent crimes throughout the state. In 2015, he assumed the position of Assistant United States Attorney for the Middle District of Alabama where he implemented the Smart on Crime initiative, served as the Re-entry Coordinator, District Elections Officer and Indian Country Liaison, and finally, Deputy Criminal Chief. In 2020, Baxley returned to the Alabama Attorney General’s Office as Chief of the Opinions Division.

“I am grateful to Governor Ivey for the trust she has placed in me by appointing me to the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals,” 
said Baxley.
 “Serving the people of Elmore County as a district court judge has been a privilege. That work has reinforced for me how much is at stake for the people who come before our courts and how important it is that every case receive careful and impartial consideration. I will bring that same commitment to the Court of Criminal Appeals and serve the people of Alabama with fairness, humility and fidelity to the law.”

A Sylacauga native, Baxley graduated from B.B. Comer High School at the age of 16 before receiving his undergraduate degree with a double major in English and History from the University of Montevallo. He earned his law degree from The University of Alabama.

Baxley’s appointment is also effective immediately. Governor Ivey will make an appointment to fill his vacancy on the District Court in Elmore County at a later date.

Governor Ivey has an impressive record appointing to the state’s highest court. With her selection of Bill Cole to the Alabama Supreme Court, this brings her total number of appointed justices to six. Most recently, she 
tapped
 Will Parker to serve on the bench.
